Grammar-Guided Generative Programming Research

Experimental pipelines combining evolutionary algorithms with subgraph mining to push structured text generation past conventional neural architectures.

Research Intern — Generative AI SystemsiCog Labs (NAC Team)Nov 2025 – Jan 2026

Overview

A research engagement exploring generative programming systems that go beyond standard transformer decoding, by constraining generation with grammars and using evolutionary search and subgraph mining to explore the structured-output space.

Problem

Conventional neural text generation is weak at reliably respecting hard structural constraints. The NAC team wanted to know whether combining evolutionary algorithms and subgraph mining with grammar-guided generation could meaningfully improve constraint adherence, and whether the approach was practical enough to inform two downstream engineering teams' roadmaps.

Solution

I built experimental grammar-guided generative programming pipelines that combined evolutionary algorithms with subgraph mining, extending structured text generation beyond what conventional neural architectures do on their own. I then evaluated the prototypes across accuracy, computational complexity, and scalability, and wrote up feasibility reports for the teams deciding whether to build on the approach.

My role

I designed the experimental pipelines, ran the benchmarking across multiple dimensions, and built reproducible experimentation and validation workflows the wider research team could reuse.

Engineering challenges

Benchmarking a genuinely new approach fairly

There wasn't an established benchmark for grammar-guided generation combined with evolutionary search, so I evaluated across accuracy, computational complexity, and scalability together rather than optimizing for a single metric that would have hidden trade-offs.

Making iteration fast enough to actually explore the space

Evolutionary search is iteration-hungry. I designed reproducible experimentation and validation pipelines specifically to cut iteration time, which is what brought experiment turnaround down by roughly 30% and made broader hypothesis testing practical within the research timeline.

Technical decisions

Reproducibility infrastructure before scaling experiments

It would have been faster short-term to run one-off scripts per experiment. I built the reproducible pipeline first because the team was going to run many variations, and that upfront investment is what paid off in the ~30% iteration-time reduction.

Results

  • ~25% improvement in output constraint adherence versus conventional neural generation baselines.
  • ~30% reduction in experimental iteration time via reproducible pipelines.
  • Feasibility reports directly influenced project prioritisation for two downstream engineering teams.
